\begin{remark}[Physics notation: BPZ conjugation]
$C$ is the conformal map from the half space to the unit ball that carries planar (Osterwalder--Schrader) quantisation to radial quantisation, and $\Theta_I$, the inversion $x\mapsto x/x^2$ with the conformal factors, is the BPZ conjugation of radial quantisation. Proposition \ref{prop:c8-primary} is the BPZ conjugate of a scalar primary of scaling dimension $w_O+\kappa$, with $\kappa=\gamma_O$ its one-loop anomalous dimension ($D_1(O)=2\kappa O$),
\[
O(x)^\dagger=|x|^{-2(w_O+\kappa)}\,\overline O\big(x/|x|^2\big),
\]
the anomalous part $K_1(O)=-2(b\cdot x)\kappa O$ of the special conformal transformation being that of $b^m\big(x^2\partial_m-2x_m\,x\cdot\partial-2(w_O+\kappa)x_m\big)$.
\end{remark}
changes.new_block:
\begin{remark}[Physics notation: BPZ conjugation]
$C$ is the conformal map from the half space to the unit ball that carries planar (Osterwalder--Schrader) quantisation to radial quantisation, and $\Theta_I$, the inversion $x\mapsto x/x^2$ with the conformal factors, is the BPZ conjugation of radial quantisation on the classical fields. $\Theta_I$ is no symmetry of the regularised theory: the heat kernel, the propagator and the mass counterterm $\tfrac94\varepsilon^{-1}$ units times $\int(A,A)$ change under the inversion. At one loop the radial conjugation is therefore the reflection $\Theta_n$ transported by the one-loop generators $P_n-K_n$ (Definition \ref{def:c8-radial}), and it depends on $P_1$ and $K_1$; $P_1=0$ is a renormalisation condition, set by the finite part $\tfrac{a_P}2\{S^{(1)}(\Delta),-\}$ of the operators when $P_1=a_P\{S^{(1)}(P_b),-\}$ (block at the end of Section 9.5). In a scheme with $P_1(O)=M_1(O)=R_1(O)=0$, Proposition \ref{prop:c8-primary} is the BPZ conjugate of a scalar primary of scaling dimension $w_O+\kappa$, with $\kappa=\gamma_O$ its one-loop anomalous dimension ($D_1(O)=2\kappa O$),
\[
O(x)^\dagger=|x|^{-2(w_O+\kappa)}\,\overline O\big(x/|x|^2\big),
\]
the anomalous part $K_1(O)=-2(b\cdot x)\kappa O$ of the special conformal transformation being that of $b^m\big(x^2\partial_m-2x_m\,x\cdot\partial-2(w_O+\kappa)x_m\big)$.
\end{remark}

changes.old_block:
\begin{remark}[Physics notation: two-point functions]
(i) is the decoupling of BRST-exact operators, (ii) the existence of the limit at separated points and the convergence at large distance, so that the endpoint is taken at $T=\infty$, and (iii) the Callan--Symanzik equation of the two-point function, with $\ell$ the renormalisation length. For a single scalar operator with $D_1(O)=2\gamma_OO$ ($\gamma_O=\frac{3g^2N}{4\pi^2}$ for the Konishi operator, $0$ for the $\mathbf{20'}$) it reads
\[
\langle O,O\rangle(x,0)=|x|^{-2w}\Big[C+(\text{one-loop finite part})-\gamma_O\,C\log\frac{|x|^2}{\ell^2}\Big],
\]
the one-loop expansion of $C\,(|x|^2/\ell^2)^{-\gamma_O}|x|^{-2w}$, the power law of an operator of dimension $w+\gamma_O$.
\end{remark}
changes.new_block:
\begin{remark}[Physics notation: two-point functions]
The two-point function of Definition \ref{def:c8-2pt} is the coefficient of $t_2t_1$ at the zero field, at tree level the free expectation $\langle O_1O_2\rangle$ with $O_1$ on the left, the ordering in which the Ward identity of Theorem \ref{thm:c8-adjoint} holds. (i) is the decoupling of BRST-exact operators, (ii) the existence of the limit at separated points and the convergence at large distance, so that the endpoint is taken at $T=\infty$, and (iii) the Callan--Symanzik equation of the two-point function, with $\ell$ the renormalisation length and the dilatation coefficients of Theorem \ref{thm:c6-dil}. For a single scalar operator with the coefficient $D_1(O)=2\gamma_OO$ ($\gamma_O=\frac{3g^2N}{4\pi^2}$ for the Konishi operator, $0$ for the $\mathbf{20'}$) it reads
\[
\langle O,O\rangle(x,0)=|x|^{-2w}\Big[C+(\text{one-loop finite part})-\gamma_O\,C\log\frac{|x|^2}{\ell^2}\Big],
\]
the one-loop expansion of $C\,(|x|^2/\ell^2)^{-\gamma_O}|x|^{-2w}$, the power law of an operator of dimension $w+\gamma_O$.
\end{remark}
